applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict, but it grounds it on the dropped curse limb rather than on a single verse's silence.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED': I weighed reading 1, limited to a stated ground of verse silence, against reading 2, barring any UNDERDETERMINED based on absence of a live contradicting link; I used reading 1.
why: The judge's stated ground is the defender's dropped curse limb and lack of any live link to contradict, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary, so K-S2 is not breached.
